newsitem.title: CANADA: Connaught hails new whooping cough vaccine.
newsitem.headline: Connaught hails new whooping cough vaccine.

text.p: Pasteur Merieux Connaught Canada said on Thursday trials of its new component pertussis vaccine against whooping cough showed it was as effective as previous whole-cell vaccines, without the unwanted side-effects that dogged the original.

Connaught, the Canadian unit of Rhone-Poulenc SA of France, said the acellular nature of the Canadian-made Pentacel vaccine caused significantly fewer reactions, like high fever, redness and pain at the injection site, than its whole-cell vaccine developed in 1943.
The new vaccineadded significant protection against mild forms of whooping cough, or pertussis, which often go undiagnosed and lead to further spread of the disease, the company said.
Connaught said moving to the new vaccine will prevent an estimated 72 percent of the existing pertussis cases in children under the age of five.

"The pertussis vaccine included in Pentacel is a breakthrough product that combats whooping cough more effectively -- and with fewer side effects -- than current pertussis vaccines," Connaught said in a statement.

Results from two trials involving more than 90,000 infants in Sweden found the component pertussis vaccine included in Pentacel to be 85 percent efficacious and to provide long-term protection in more than 80 percent of cases.

Pentacel is the first single-injection combination vaccine to include a designer vaccine that provides improved protection against pertussis. It also contains four other vaccines for protection against diphtheria, tetanus, polio and Haemophilus influenza type B.
Connaught said its main focus is the Canadian market but it is seeking licenses in another 26 countries. In Canada, about two million doses of Pentacel will be needed every year.
